exposure: Mode of labor management (elective induction vs. expectant management)
outcome: Rate of third- or fourth-degree lacerations
Neonatal intensive care unit admission rate
cohort: Nulliparous women with a vertex singleton gestation, a body mass index of 30.0 kg/m2 or greater at delivery, and an unfavorable cervix (modified Bishop score <5) between 38.0 and 38.9 weeks of gestation who delivered at MedStar Washington Hospital Center from 2007 to 2012.
finding: Elective labor induction at term in obese nulliparous patients with an unfavorable cervix is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery and higher neonatal intensive care unit admission rate compared to expectant management.
mod_finding: Elective labor induction at term in obese nulliparous patients with an unfavorable cervix is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery compared to expectant management.
gest_age: 39.0 and 40.9 weeks' gestation (induction group) and beyond 39.0 weeks (expectant management group)
